profiles.name: Single course
profiles.purpose: Onboard and build one course. CXS (the context shell) runs first, pre, before the agent authors anything. The query layers then narrow the context top-down (tier, levels, generic statements) and AO-01 builds the course's learning outcomes, flat (settled 2 Nov 2026: no separate course-outcome tier) and not fixed at 6 (revised 2 Nov 2026: typically 4-6, content shape decides the count). AO-04 turns AO-01 into the ONB shell statement that feeds the course body. Once the shell and lessons exist, CXP (the context pack) runs standalone, post (settled 2 Nov 2026: cxs before crs, cxp after) - and getting this working is a priority, not an optional extra: fork02-shell lets the human assign the whole course to a HESA/CAH subject grouping, from one large discipline (a whole CAH1 such as Computing) down to one specific HECoS subject or Cardiff Met course/programme, via the existing tools/resolve-subject-benchmark.js resolver; ao-02 then generates context-specific competency attributes and worked examples grounded in that subject's QAA benchmark, merged into the shell's reserved slots via merge-context.js. The same resolver can also be used early, inside ctx-shell, when the discipline is already known at onboarding. The run records the tiers and levels the course could feed into or build from, but builds only this one.
profiles.produces: One course at one tier and level band: AO-04 shell context statement, flat learning outcomes (typically 4-6), a lesson map of up to 6 lessons (one LO each, circa 4-6 pages per lesson), the course build, then a standalone context pack - baseline, a whole discipline, or one specific subject/course - merged into the shell with subject-grounded examples.

Per-school shortlist (built, verified against the live resolver 2 Nov 2026): docs/contexts/cmet/cardiff_met_school_hesa_shortlist.json pairs each of the 5 schools (cardiff_met_schools.json) with its own top 6-10 commonly-picked HESA/CAH groupings, so choosing a school offers a short list instead of the full CAH tree; cardiff_met_courses.csv (239 courses) grounds which real Cardiff Met courses sit inside each grouping

steps.produces: the shell's subject grounding: baseline, or a resolved subject-benchmark reference (id + file in catalogue/context/subject/benchmarks.json) at whichever level the human picks - a whole discipline (group) or one course/subject (specific). This is a working priority for CXP, not an optional extra.
steps.open: tools/resolve-subject-benchmark.js and the CAH1-3/HECoS resolver already exist and do this lookup end to end; the per-school shortlist file now exists. It found and documents a real catalogue gap worth human sign-off on: several of csshs's dominant subjects (sport and exercise science, nursing, midwifery, physiotherapy, podiatry, dietetics, speech and language therapy) have no dedicated entry in the 55-entry catalogue/context/subject/benchmarks.json yet, so a bare CAH1/CAH2 pick for those either returns no benchmark or, worse, silently falls back to an unrelated entry that merely shares the same CAH2 ancestor (e.g. nursing resolves to optometry-2024) - the shortlist file flags each entry's matchQuality (direct | umbrella | fallback-imprecise) so fork02-shell's human gate can see which picks are trustworthy as-is.

profiles.name: Pathway distillation (all three tiers)
profiles.purpose: Distil a whole pathway for all three tiers at once, and - the point of this profile right now - give the agent and human a single view across all three tiers together, so the progression between them (what introductory sets up, what advanced builds on) can be seen and designed, not just inferred lesson-by-lesson. CXS runs first, pre, shared across all three tiers; CXP (post, subject/discipline grounding) runs once after all three tiers' lessons exist, same priority as in single-course - one resolved HESA/CAH subject or discipline context pack, shared across the tiers since the subject does not change tier to tier. The 18 pathway statements (two evidence examples for each of the 9 capabilities, so 6 per tier) are evolved into each tier's flat learning outcomes (settled 2 Nov 2026: no course-outcome distillation, no lesson-outcome expansion; revised 2 Nov 2026: not fixed at 6 per tier either - typically 4-6, content shape decides) and mapped one-to-one onto up to 6 lessons per tier, each carrying circa 4-6 pages to develop its one LO well. Every outcome traces back to its source statement(s) in the 18. Once all three tiers' outcomes and lesson maps exist, a dedicated progression step reviews them side by side and adds the forward/backward signposting between tiers.
profiles.produces: For each of introductory, intermediate and advanced: flat learning outcomes (typically 4-6) and a lesson map of up to 6 lessons (one LO each), plus a cross-tier progression map (forward and backward signposts between the three tiers), plus one shared subject/discipline context pack (baseline, a whole discipline, or one specific subject) merged into all three tiers' shells.

steps.label: Flat learning outcomes per tier, book-first, 5-6 per tier
inputs: source-kb/source-maps/book-excelling-at-university-2026.json: the pathway's book chapter, chunked and tagged (sectionKind, pathwayTags, content-shapes[])
the tier's 6 statements (the capability+evidence pairs keyed to this tier)
tierReadings and the tier's section 16 verb band
the benchmarks keyed to the tier
steps.produces: the tier's learning outcomes, flat, each traced either to a book section, a benchmark statement, or a named theory source - settled 2 Nov 2026, method revised same day (supersedes the merge/cluster rule below, which tested negative on two pathways - see crs-redesign.md's referencing run, 6/6/6 with zero merges). Two-layer method, agent proposes / human gates: Layer 1 (primary) - one LO per real section of the pathway's own book chapter, as many as the book naturally gives; the book's cross-references and definitions take precedence over external theory. Layer 2 (secondary, fill-to-minimum only) - where Layer 1 falls short of 5 LOs, fill using (a) the pathway's own applied/professional benchmark evidence (no new theory), and/or (b) at most one named theory lesson PER TIER (each tier is its own Adapt course, so each tier carries its own theory budget), delivered anchored inside an existing book-grounded lesson's context, never freestanding. Worked example: criticality settled at 5/5/6 LOs (introductory/intermediate/advanced) - see crs-redesign.md's 'Worked example - criticality' section for the full traced table.
steps.open: the statement-merge rule is superseded as the generative mechanism (book section count drives it instead) but not yet deleted as a concept - still open whether it survives as a tie-breaker for an unusually long book section list. Also open: the exact Layer-2 trigger logic beyond 'fill to 5' - e.g. whether a tier that is short by two LOs takes two benchmark fills, one fill plus the theory lesson, or the theory lesson alone, is an agent judgement call per run, not yet a rule.

steps.label: 5-6 lessons per tier (hard floor 5, ceiling 6), one LO each
steps.change: settled 2 Nov 2026: no crs-03_course-outcomes distillation and no lesson-outcome expansion step, per tier. The tier's flat LOs (5-6, set by tiered-outcomes' book-first two-layer method) map one-to-one onto 5-6 lessons, each circa 4-6 pages deep (the six-part flow). A synthesis lesson is optional colour, not a structural 3-vs-6 slot. crs-03_course-outcomes has no job left in this flow.
steps.produces: 5-6 lessons per tier, one LO each (minimum 5 enforced 2 Nov 2026; ceiling remains 6)
steps.open: crs-04's dependency note and every lesson's serves field assume a course-outcome id (design-kb.gates.json:748-755); wra-03's AL-3 rule (two summative questions per course outcome, design-kb.gates.json:1361-1366) has no course outcome to count against - open whether it becomes two-per-LO (10-12) or one-per-LO (5-6) per tier. crs-03_course-outcomes itself needs removing or repurposing before this touches live gates.

steps.label: Progression review: all three tiers, side by side

all three tiers' lesson maps (lessons, introductory + intermediate + advanced together)
steps.produces: the cross-tier progression: for each tier, a forward signpost (what this tier sets up for the next one up) and a backward signpost (what this tier assumes or builds on from the one below). Not a new gate on its own content - it reads and annotates the three tiers' existing outcomes/lesson maps once all three exist.

First attempt at a dedicated 'view all three tiers at once' step - still to decide: does the signpost attach per LO, per lesson, or per tier as a whole; does it change the LO/lesson text itself or sit alongside it as a separate annotation; is there a UI for the human to see all three tiers in one pass, or is this agent-drafted prose the human reads linearly.
